scope: Guard the existing Storyboard failure state transition by organization, current workflow identity and terminal status in one database statement.

beforeAfter.before: Storyboard read mutable status, then wrote failed unconditionally. A completed result, specific child failure or newer run could win between the two operations and still be overwritten.
beforeAfter.after: One conditional UPDATE checks sequence, organization, current run ownership and nonterminal status; false skips the parent failure event.

beforeAfter.before: Only using the actual workflow instance id would miss the launcher raw claim before the final instance-id write-back.
beforeAfter.after: The launcher snapshots its acquired claim onto the internal payload after resolving user input; failure cleanup matches either this trusted claim or the actual instance id without decoding ids.

beforeAfter.before: A trigger exception marked the sequence failed without checking whether its claim still owned it.
beforeAfter.after: The launcher exception path uses the same guard with its raw claim and preserves its original error, logging and run.failed activity behavior.

preservedContracts: failed and completed rows keep their original status, statusError and updatedAt; newer run owners are not modified.
A true result means this call changed the current nonterminal sequence to failed. Guard misses, repeated failure, absent rows, null owners and foreign organizations return false.
Storyboard ordinary guard errors still allow an independent notification attempt and then reject with the first error; surfaced engine aborts stop later actions.
Reservation release and launcher status cleanup remain best effort for ordinary errors. The launcher rethrows its original trigger error even when guard persistence fails.
Old payloads lacking workflowClaimId may match the actual instance id only; no raw claim is guessed. New launcher calls always overwrite the field with the acquired claim.
runImpl orchestration and success/startup writes, model configuration snapshots, pricing, organization permissions and public API/MCP schemas are unchanged.

productionCallSites.purpose: onFailure passes actual instance id and optional trusted claim; emits only after a guard hit, or as the preserved fallback when the guard throws an ordinary error.
Trusted claim snapshot at dispatch and guarded failure cleanup on a trigger exception, before the final instance id is known.

originalAssertionTreatment: Mutable-status read assertions were migrated because that action no longer exists. Real DB tests now preserve the completed/child-failed and newer-owner protections. Hook mocks still pin guard parameters, reservation best effort, guard miss suppression, first-error propagation and engine abort. The test section from makeStep through all runImpl tests was compared with sourceBefore and is byte-identical after CRLF normalization. The exact launcher payload snapshot was extended with the acquired workflowClaimId rather than loosened.
alternativeAssessment: A workflow-side reread or outer catch cannot make the status check and write atomic. Reuse the existing scoped DB and launcher ownership protocol; add one internal snapshot field because raw claims and transformed platform ids differ. No parallel lifecycle implementation or ID parsing was added.
compatibilityRisks: Upstream changes to workflow slot acquisition, instance-id generation, terminal statuses, organization scoping or launcher dispatch/write-back require reviewing all four production integration points.
The guard is a bounded database fix, not completion of the full lifecycle, event delivery or frozen responsibility inventory.
newEvidence: Six behavior failures in the nine-case real DB/hook composition baseline before production changes.

Sixteen new real createTestDb cases combine actual migrations and domain DB methods with an explicit partial WorkflowScopedDb, event and channel stub; SQL errors are injected by a test-only synthetic trigger.
The three directly affected suites passed 84 tests; the selected integration command passed 26 files and 384 tests.
